notes.content: The scar on Aldric's wrist glows faintly in the moonlight. Ysara had not noticed it before. It is the shape of a broken circle, and when she looks at it, she feels a sadness so deep it makes her breath catch.
needle_syns: the scar glows in the moonlight

notes.content: She asks him about the scar. He turns his wrist away and says, 'An old injury.' She does not push. Some things are not meant to be known, at least not yet. She turns her face away and looks at the moon instead.
needle_syns: he said it was an old injury
some things are not meant to be known

notes.content: In the village, children play in the street. They are playing a game where they pretend to be soldiers, and one of them is pretending to be dead, lying in the dirt with his eyes closed. Ysara watches and feels a pain in her chest that she does not understand.

An old woman from the village comes up to Ysara and touches her arm. 'You have walked a long way,' the woman says. Ysara says yes. The woman says, 'You have a long way to go.' She does not say more, and she walks away.
needle_syns: you have walked a long way
you have a long way to go

notes.content: Ysara thinks about the old woman's words. 'You have walked a long way.' That is true. 'You have a long way to go.' That is true too. But the woman did not mean the road. She meant something else, something that Ysara will understand later, much later, when it is too late to change it.
needle_syns: the woman did not mean the road

notes.content: As they leave the village, Ysara looks back. The stone people are still there, frozen in their laughter and arguments and prayers. They will always be there. The frost pact has left its mark on this place, and the mark will never go away.
needle_syns: the stone people are still there
the mark will never go away

notes.content: Ysara makes a promise to the stone people. She promises that they will not be stone forever. She does not know how she will do it, but she promises anyway, because that is what you do for people who have been turned to stone by a cruel spell.
needle_syns: promises they will not be stone forever

notes.content: Aldric hears her promise. He does not say anything, but his face changes. It becomes harder, more like the stone people. She thinks he is angry, but she is not sure why. Maybe he is afraid of what she is promising.

That night, they camp in a field. The stars are very bright, brighter than they have been before. Ysara lies on her back and watches them, and she thinks about the old woman's words and the stone people and the promise she made. She feels very small under the stars.
needle_syns: she feels very small under the stars

notes.content: Ysara sings to the stars. She sings the lullaby from the frost hall, and the stars seem to listen. They seem to lean closer, as if they are trying to understand. She sings until her voice is gone, and then she is silent, and the stars are silent too.
When she stops singing, she realizes Aldric is asleep. He is sleeping peacefully for the first time since they started walking. She hopes the stars did not wake him. She hopes the stars are kind.
needle_syns: she hopes the stars are kind

notes.content: On the third day, rain begins to fall. Ysara has never seen rain — in the frost hall, water only exists as ice. She puts her hand out and catches the drops, and they feel like tiny cold kisses on her skin.
needle_syns: the rain felt like tiny cold kisses
she catches the drops in her hand

notes.content: Aldric stands in the rain without moving. The water does not seem to bother him. He stands there for a long time, letting it run down his face, and Ysara wonders if he is washing something away.
needle_syns: he lets the rain run down his face

notes.content: Ysara is hungry. She has not eaten in two days because they ran out of bread. Aldric has a piece of dried meat in his pack, and he offers it to her without being asked. She takes it and eats it gratefully, and it tastes like leather, but it is food.
needle_syns: the dried meat tastes like leather

notes.content: She is thirstier than she is hungry. Her throat is dry and her lips are cracked. Aldric gives her his waterskin, and she drinks until she can drink no more. The water is cold and tastes like metal, but it is water.
needle_syns: drinks until she cannot drink more

notes.content: They reach a river. It is not very wide, but it is deep and fast. There is no bridge. Aldric wades in without hesitation, and the water rises to his waist. He waits for her on the other side.
needle_syns: he waits for her on the other side

notes.content: Ysara crosses the river by herself. The current is strong and it pulls at her legs, but she keeps going. When she reaches the other side, she is shaking, but she is alive, and Aldric nods to her once, which is his way of saying good job.
needle_syns: her way of saying good job

notes.content: After the crossing, Ysara feels different. She is colder, but she is also stronger, as if the river has given her something. She does not know what, but she knows it is there, inside her, waiting.
needle_syns: the river has given her something

notes.content: They meet a hermit in the woods. He lives in a cave and he grows mushrooms. He gives them a bowl of mushroom soup and tells them about the road ahead. 'The road gets harder,' he says. 'But it also gets more beautiful.'

Ysara asks the hermit what he means by 'more beautiful.' He smiles and says, 'You will know when you see it.' She does not like the answer, but the hermit will not say more. He has said what he is going to say, and now he wants them to leave.
needle_syns: you will know when you see it

notes.content: As they leave the hermit's cave, Ysara looks back. The hermit is watching them go. He raises his hand and waves, and Ysara waves back. She wonders if she will ever see him again. She hopes so, because the mushroom soup was the best thing she has ever eaten.
needle_syns: she hopes to see him again
the best thing she has ever eaten

notes.content: That night, they camp near a stream. The water is clear and Ysara can see the bottom, the stones and the sand and the tiny creatures that swim between them. She watches them for a long time, fascinated.
needle_syns: tiny creatures that swim between them

notes.content: In her sleep, Ysara dreams of a farm. Not a battle or a fortress, but a farm with animals and fields and a big red barn. In the dream, she is not a mage or a knight. She is just a girl, and she is happy. When she wakes up, she is crying, but she does not know why.
needle_syns: she is just a girl in the dream

notes.content: Aldric finds her crying in the morning. He asks what is wrong. She says she does not know. She says she had a dream, but she does not remember what it was about. He does not press her. He just sits beside her until she stops crying.
needle_syns: she does not remember the dream
he sits beside her until she stops crying

needle_syns: she wishes they could turn back

notes.content: At night, Ysara sees the first star. It is a single bright star, and it is so big and so close that she thinks it might be falling. She watches it for a long time, and it does not fall. It just stays there, shining down on them like a watchful eye.
needle_syns: the star shines like a watchful eye

notes.content: Ysara talks to the star. She tells it about the stone people and the promise she made. She tells it about the hermit and the mushroom soup. needle_syns: she says the man who walks with me

notes.content: After that, Ysara talks to the stars every night. She tells them everything, about her fears and her hopes and her confusion. She tells them about the war she does not understand and the enemy she has not seen. The stars listen, and that is enough for her.
needle_syns: she talks to the stars every night
the stars listen and that is enough

notes.content: Aldric hears her talking to the stars. He does not mind. In fact, he seems glad, because when she is talking to the stars, she is not talking to him, and he does not have to answer. He just lies there in the dark, listening, and he does not know if he should be glad or sad.

he does not have to answer

needle_syns: the thing that will stop us
he is looking at something she cannot see

notes.content: The night before they reach the bridge, Ysara finds a feather. It is a blue feather, and it is very soft. She picks it up and puts it in her pocket. She does not know where it came from, but she keeps it, and it makes her feel less afraid.
needle_syns: it makes her feel less afraid

notes.content: For the rest of the journey, Ysara carries the blue feather in her pocket. She touches it when she is afraid, and it helps a little. She does not know why it helps, but it does. It is the only thing from the outside world that she owns.
needle_syns: she touches it when she is afraid
the only thing she owns from the outside world

notes.content: One day, the feather falls out of her pocket. She looks for it, but she cannot find it. The road is wide, and the feather is small. It is gone, and she will never find it again. She feels sad, but she keeps walking.
needle_syns: she will never find it again

notes.content: For the rest of the journey, Ysara misses the feather. She puts her hand in her pocket often, expecting to feel it, but it is not there. She does not tell Aldric about it. It is too small a thing to tell anyone about.
needle_syns: she puts her hand in her pocket often
it is too small a thing to tell anyone

needle_syns: the reflection looking back at her
